headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% for a Fourth Time as Q4 GDP Contracts 0.6% and Oil Hits $100 on the Strait of Hormuz Disruption
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25%1 on April 29, 2026, a fourth consecutive hold and unchanged since October 2025. Governing Council said it would look through the war's immediate inflation impact but "will not let higher energy prices become persistent inflation," projecting a return to the 2% target in 2027.2 The prime rate stands at 6.09%. The database tracks 211 residential projects ($32.2B) and 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3B) carrying rate-sensitive financing; the next scheduled decision is June 10, 2026.1

Real GDP contracted -0.6% annualized in the fourth quarter of 2025 against a consensus expectation of flat output, and full-year 2025 growth was 1.7%, the slowest pace since 2016 excluding the pandemic, according to Statistics Canada.10 Lower exports, particularly to the U.S. under steel, aluminum and motor-vehicle tariffs, were the main drag. Manufacturing GDP fell 3.1% year-over-year; the database tracks 83 manufacturing projects ($129.0B), and StatCan reported three in ten manufacturers cited a major negative tariff impact with one in five planning to delay investment.10

WTI crude settled near US$100.16/bbl (+5.0% on the week, +60.1% year-over-year) and Brent at US$108.59 (+7.2% on the week) as the Strait of Hormuz disruption cut roughly 4 million barrels per day of flows in March and April; the IEA described the disruption as exceeding the 1970s oil crises in scale.20 The energy move fed inflation: headline CPI rose 2.4% year-over-year in March, up from 1.8% in February, lifted by a record 21.2% month-over-month gasoline increase, and remained within the Bank of Canada's 1-3% target band.5 The database tracks 59 oil_gas projects ($97.6B).

Canada posted a $1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March, its first since September 2025, reversing a $5.1B February deficit, as exports to the U.S. rose 8.3% and non-U.S. exports hit an all-time high (+9.1% month-over-month).13 Unemployment rose to 6.9% in April from 6.7% in March, with 18,000 jobs lost and youth unemployment at 14.3%.7 The week ahead brings the April CPI and housing-starts prints on May 17, the Q1 2026 national accounts in late May, and the next Bank of Canada decision on June 10.5

national.analysis:
Canada's real GDP contracted at an annualized rate of -0.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025 against a consensus expectation of flat output, and full-year 2025 growth was 1.7%, the slowest pace since 2016 excluding the pandemic, according to Statistics Canada.10 Lower exports, particularly to the U.S. under steel, aluminum and motor-vehicle tariffs, were the main 2025 drag. StatCan reported that three in ten manufacturers cited a major negative tariff impact and one in five plan to delay investment.10

Industry GDP movements were mixed. Manufacturing output fell 3.1% year-over-year (NAICS 31-33) even as it rose 1.8% on the month; the database tracks 83 manufacturing projects ($129.0B).10 Mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction (NAICS 21) rose 0.4% month-over-month and 3.6% year-over-year, with 390 projects ($227.1B) tracked. Construction (NAICS 23) declined 0.5% month-over-month, while transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) rose 1.2% month-over-month and 4.5% year-over-year, aligning with 612 transport_logistics projects ($44.1B). Management of companies (NAICS 55) recorded a 22.3% year-over-year decline and utilities (NAICS 22) fell 4.0% year-over-year.

The Labour Force Survey recorded unemployment at 6.9% in April, up 0.2 percentage points from 6.7% in March, as the economy shed 18,000 positions.7 Youth unemployment reached 14.3% and the long-term unemployment share was 22.5%. The employment rate eased to 60.5% while participation held at 65.0%. Indeed Hiring Lab characterized the labour market as "stuck in neutral."8 SEPH wage growth ran at +3.9% year-over-year on a February reference, and The Hub reported 112,000 private-sector jobs lost year-to-date in 2026 alongside public-sector hiring cuts.9

Canada posted a $1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March, its first since September 2025, reversing a $5.1B February deficit, a $6.9B swing.13 The surplus with the U.S. widened to $7.1B as exports to the U.S. rose 8.3%, led by crude oil and passenger vehicles, while non-U.S. exports hit an all-time high (+9.1% month-over-month) on metal, mineral and energy products. The database tracks 390 mining projects ($227.1B) and 59 oil_gas projects ($97.6B).

CMHC's March housing-starts monthly SAAR fell 6% to 235,852 units from 250,961 in February, with the six-month trend easing to 248,378.16 Actual starts in centres of 10,000 or more population were 16,398 units, +10% year-over-year, with Montreal +26%, Toronto +23% and Vancouver +21% on multi-unit construction. Headline CPI rose 2.4% year-over-year in March, up from 1.8% in February, on a record 21.2% month-over-month gasoline increase; core CPI median ran at 2.3%, shelter +1.5% and food 5.3%.5 The database tracks 211 residential projects ($32.2B) and 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3B) carrying rate-sensitive financing while the Bank of Canada holds at 2.25%.

consumer_pulse:
Cost-of-living attention concentrated on gasoline. The national average pump price rose to $1.92/L on May 12 from $1.87/L on May 5, about +3% in a week, with Newfoundland and Labrador highest at $2.09/L and Alberta lowest at $1.79/L.30 StatCan's March gasoline component rose a record 21.2% month-over-month and 5.9% year-over-year.5 Reddit and Google Trends signals tracked "gas prices" (sentiment -0.7, frequency 19), "oil shock / Middle East war" (-0.6), "inflation" (-0.5) and "cost of living" (-0.6) as the dominant themes.

Wages have outpaced prices for more than three years, with SEPH wage growth at +3.9% year-over-year, partially offsetting cost pressure.9 Rental affordability shifted: the national rent-to-income ratio fell to 29%, below the 30% threshold for the first time in more than six years, and average rent declined 5.3% year-over-year to $2,008.32 The lowest five-year fixed mortgage rate was about 4.04%, edging up as energy-driven inflation lifts fixed rates; CIBC reported 70% of prospective buyers say conditions are too uncertain to judge timing.31 Labour-market unease registered in trending topics on "jobs lost" (frequency 14), "youth unemployment" and "layoffs" after April recorded 18,000 jobs lost, unemployment at 6.9%, youth unemployment at 14.3% and a long-term unemployment share of 22.5%.7 "U.S. tariffs" (frequency 15) and "economic uncertainty" (frequency 14) remained persistent threads.

global.analysis: The Federal Reserve held the fed funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29, 2026, a third consecutive hold, with the FOMC statement citing elevated inflation "in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices."23 The meeting was Chair Powell's likely final one, with Kevin Warsh's appointment effective May 15, 2026, and markets pricing no Fed changes through the rest of 2026 and into 2027.24 U.S. GDP ran at +2.0% for Q4 2025 with CPI at +3.9% and unemployment at 4.3%. The wide Fed-BoC differential (3.50%-3.75% versus 2.25%) accompanies a softer Canadian dollar despite high crude prices, and U.S. growth sustains Canadian export demand even amid steel, aluminum and motor-vehicle tariffs.

global.analysis: China's Q1 2026 GDP rose +5.0%, up from +4.5% in Q4 2025 and above the roughly 4.8% consensus, at the top of the 4.5-5% target band.25 The March official manufacturing PMI was 50.4 (+1.4 points month-over-month, expansionary), while the Caixin/RatingDog manufacturing reading softened to 50.8 from 52.1, and the Middle East war lifted input costs into China factory data.26 CPI ran at +0.1% with unemployment at 4.6% and the policy rate at 2.90%. Resilient Chinese demand accompanies copper at +37.3% year-over-year in the timeseries, alongside iron ore and energy export prices; the potash and canola channel is relevant qualitatively, with no timeseries series tracked this run.

global.analysis: The European Central Bank held all three key rates on April 30, 2026, with the deposit rate at 2.00%, the MRO at 2.15% and marginal lending at 2.40%.27 Bloomberg-surveyed economists expect two ECB quarter-point hikes in 2026, in June and September, as the war drives inflation higher, placing the energy-driven global inflation regime in focus.28 EU GDP ran at +0.2% with HICP at +1.9% and unemployment at 6.2%. Prospective ECB tightening accompanies a firmer euro and higher global yields, aligning with the back-up in Government of Canada yields of roughly 5-7 basis points on the week.

global.analysis: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on April 30, 2026, a second consecutive hold and a third decision without a cut, with the Monetary Policy Committee voting 8-1.29 The decision confirms a synchronized G7 hold stance through April amid the energy shock. UK GDP ran at +0.1% with CPI at +3.4% and unemployment at 5.2%. The synchronized G7 hold and energy-shock backdrop accompany global term-premium repricing, reflected in higher Government of Canada yields of roughly 5-7 basis points on the week.
